jp: 先週[せんしゅう]、山口[やまぐち]さん{という|toiu-called}新[あたら]しい社員[しゃいん]{が|ga-subject}入[はい]りました。
en: Last week a new employee called Ms. Yamaguchi joined.
why: X という N says that N is called X; と would make a list, and を or が cannot link the two nouns.

jp: 「経済学[けいざいがく]」{という|toiu-called}授業[じゅぎょう]{を|o-object}取[と]っています。
en: I am taking a class called Economics.
why: という attaches the name to the noun class, meaning 'a class called Economics'.

jp: 今日[きょう]{の|no-possessive}授業[じゅぎょう]{で|de-place}「敬語[けいご]」{という|toiu-called}言葉[ことば]{を|o-object}習[なら]いました。
en: In today's class we learned the word 'keigo'.
why: という introduces the name of the word being learned, 'a word called keigo'.

jp: 来年[らいねん]{から|kara-from}「プログラミング」{という|toiu-called}科目[かもく]{が|ga-subject}始[はじ]まります。
en: From next year, a subject called Programming will start.
why: The name of the subject comes before という and the noun it names follows.

jp: 部長[ぶちょう]{は|wa-topic}「毎日[まいにち]早[はや]く来[く]る」{という|toiu-called}ルール{を|o-object}作[つく]りました。
en: The manager made a rule that everyone must come in early every day.
why: という links a whole clause to the noun rule, giving its content: the rule that people come early.

jp: アルバイト先[さき]{に|ni-location}佐藤[さとう]さん{という|toiu-called}優[やさ]しい先輩[せんぱい]{が|ga-existence}います。
en: At my part-time job there is a kind senior colleague called Mr. Sato.
why: Name + という + noun says that the person is called Mr. Sato; a list with と changes the meaning.
